evals.prompt: Прадед Мордко Коган умер в 1913 году в местечке Чуднов Волынской губернии. Можно ли найти его могилу и что на ней может быть написано такого, чего нет в метриках?
evals.expected_output: First checks whether the cemetery exists and survives: the JewishGen Cemetery Discovery Project (Ukraine → Chudnov) and the ESJF page (fenced, about 300 stones, the oldest from 1885, the newest from 1939, GPS); ESJF has no name index. Searches for the burial in JOWBR (a human does the login), Mitzvat Emet (beginning of the surname, choose the suggestion, no more than about 5 searches in a row, do not bypass the CAPTCHA) and Toldot; tries the spellings Коган/Kogan/Cohen and Мордко/Мордехай/Марк (Mordko/Mordechai/Mark). Explains what the stone gives: the father's name (בן), הכהן meaning Kohen descent, the hands symbol, the date in the Jewish calendar, whether the father was alive or dead (נ״י / ז״ל). If the databases have nothing, a photo on site can be taken by the person or a volunteer; only the person makes the arrangements. States a negative result with a list of databases, spellings and the status of the cemetery, without concluding "not buried there".

evals.prompt: Прочитай, пожалуйста, надпись с надгробия (переписала с фото): פ״נ / האשה החשובה / מרת שרה רבקה / בת ר׳ יצחק ז״ל / נפ׳ י״ב כסלו / תרס״ה לפ״ק / ת.נ.צ.ב.ה. Сверху вырезаны два подсвечника. Что это даёт?
evals.expected_output: Reads it line by line: here lies buried; the esteemed woman, Mrs., so married; the name Sarah-Rivka (a double name is one name); daughter of reb Yitzchak, where ר׳ is the polite "reb", not a rabbi; ז״ל means the father had died by this time; died 12 Kislev; תרס״ה = 5665 by the small count; ת.נ.צ.ב.ה. is the standard formula. Converts the date: Kislev is an autumn month, so the year is 1904, not 1905; by Hebcal 20 November 1904 (Gregorian), and for Russian documents 7 November 1904 in the Julian calendar. The candlesticks are a woman's symbol. Conclusions for the search: the father's name (Yitzchak = Itsko/Isaak) is a step up one generation, and his death was before November 1904; she was married, so look for the husband among the neighbouring stones and for the death record. Offers to fill in gravestone-record.md and to check the reading against the photo.

evals.prompt: My great-grandfather is buried in a cemetery in Queens, in a section with a gate that has a society name on it, something like 'First Zhitomirer Benevolent Society'. Nobody remembers which town the family came from. Does the cemetery help?
evals.expected_output: Explains that landsmanshaft plots were bought by societies of immigrants from one town, so the society section points to the likely town of origin (here Zhitomir or its district) as a hypothesis. Searches JGSNY's burial society database by society name or town (3+ characters; over 10,600 entries from about 100 New York-area cemeteries) and checks the plot maps; recommends reading the gate and the gravestone in full — the Hebrew side gives the father's name, Kohen/Levi status and the Hebrew date. Suggests Find a Grave and BillionGraves for photos and JOWBR, and confirming the town through naturalization papers, manifests and the society's records (tracing-emigrants-to-origin). States that burial in a society plot is evidence, not proof — members sometimes joined societies of other towns — and that only the user arranges photo requests or contacts with the cemetery.
